item.title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
item.description: arXiv:2610.37730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Unnikrishna Pillai

item.title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.37990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact divisibility relations and the factorization $\Tst=\TG\,m$, where $m$ counts the applications of the symmetry $h$ that maps the configuration onto itself after $\TG$ steps: $\TG$ and the type of $h$ belong to the pattern, $m$ to the lattice, and the attractors are relative periodic orbits whose full period emerges from the interaction between the intrinsic dynamics and the lattice symmetries. A family of attractors built around a pair of counter-rotating spirals, with $\Tpop=24$ and $\TG=8$, persists from $L=9$ to $L=40$ while $\Tst$ takes values from 24 to 960, given in every case by the order of $h$; on a rectangular $9\times12$ torus it takes the value 48, absent from all square tori. With more than $4.5\times10^5$ runs at each of $L=8$ and $L=9$ we estimate the basins of attraction: fixed points take 95--97\% of the configuration space, and no single period is enough to tell the oscillating attractors apart. The same analysis locates local diversity: it is balanced whenever the cycle has a color symmetry and, on large lattices, it is concentrated at the spiral cores.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no

item.title: Strong stable sets and asymptotic fineness
item.description: arXiv:2610.38099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the strong stable sets of the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces and their relation to the injectivity radius. We prove that the strong stable set of a vector does not coincide with its stable horocycle if and only if the injectivity radius along the associated geodesic ray is not bounded away from zero and the ray does not diverge through a cusp. In that case, the strong stable set is an uncountable union of stable horocycles. In previous works, we considered the particular cases where the ray meets arbitrarily short closed geodesics or closed horocycles. Here we complete the study by treating the third possible case, where the ray meets closed hypercycles of arbitrarily small length.
item.dc:creator: Sergi Burniol Clotet, Fran\c{c}oise Dal'Bo

item.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
item.description: arXiv:2610.38374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.
item.dc:creator: Beldiman Miruna-Mihaela, Halanay Andrei-Dan

item.title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. We test the method on a stochastic pitchfork model and a spatial stochastic Swift-Hohenberg equation. In both models, classification improves with longer observation horizons, closer proximity to the bifurcation, stronger noise, and larger nonlinear effects. However, these conditions are also linked to a higher risk of noise-induced tipping in the subcritical case. The useful early-warning window is therefore determined by a balance between obtaining enough information to identify the bifurcation type and doing so before noise-induced tipping becomes too likely. In spatially extended systems, we find that observing the full spatial field allows classification over shorter observation horizons, and performance improves when a broader range of spatial modes contributes to the observed dynamics. Altogether, we identify the conditions under which the method can reliably distinguish between supercritical and subcritical bifurcations.
item.dc:creator: Paul A. Sanders, Christian Kuehn, Bastian Hilder, Robbin Bastiaansen

item.title: Networks with Memory and Isospectral Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.38995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Restricting the linear dynamics of a graph to selected vertices generally introduces memory, because interactions can pass through hidden vertices before returning. The resulting rational memory kernels give isospectral reduction a dynamical interpretation and identify latent graph symmetries with symmetries of the observed evolution.
item.dc:creator: Grant Molnar

item.title: Frequency-induced Tipping: Resonance-Driven Tipping in a Threshold Predator-Prey System
item.description: arXiv:2610.39113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tipping points refer to abrupt, substantial, and often irreversible transitions in dynamic systems that can be triggered by minor perturbations. Existing tipping mechanisms are usually classified by the nature of the trigger: bifurcation-induced tipping occurs when a parameter crosses a critical threshold, noise-induced tipping is caused by random perturbations, rate-induced tipping occurs when a system fails to track a moving attractor, and phase-induced tipping is triggered by timed perturbations relative to an oscillatory state. In this paper, we identify a new mechanism for tipping: frequency-induced tipping, in which periodic forcing drives a transition through resonant amplification. This occurs by destabilization of an equilibrium via subthreshold perturbations of the appropriate frequency. Filippov analysis of a piecewise-smooth model identifies admissible crossings that lead either to predator loss or to extinction of predator and prey, and numerical simulations show that tipping persists after smoothing of the thresholds. These results extend the current tipping framework to include critical transitions under recurrent environmental forcing.
item.dc:creator: Shan Gao, Silas Poloni, Hao Wang, Mark Lewis

item.title: Dynamic invisibility of implicit and nested state-dependent delays in a class of externally forced delay equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delayed feedback is a fundamental mechanism in many systems and is often modeled by delay differential equations (DDEs). While delays are frequently assumed to be constant, in realistic feedback processes they may depend on the state and even be defined implicitly or in a nested fashion by the feedback relation itself. In this work, we address the question of how such implicit and nested state-dependent delays affect the observed behavior of a class of externally forced systems with negative switched feedback. Our motivating example and principal case study is the piecewise-smooth limiting form of a conceptual DDE model for the El Ni\~no-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) with a negative feedback term subject to implicit state-dependent delay. We prove, for a wider prototypical class of DDEs with switched negative feedback and more general forcing, that (subject to an explicit condition on the parameters) any finite level of nested state-dependent delay and the limiting implicit delay are dynamically invisible: they all generate exactly the same trajectory, namely, that of the corresponding constant-delay DDE. We also discuss how the delayed argument functions organize the temporal order of reactions (TOR) in this regime, and show that a more stringent condition is required to ensure TOR for nested state-dependent delays.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Bolduc-St-Aubin, Priya Subramanian, Bernd Krauskopf

item.title: The entropy spectra of chaotic maps of an interval
item.description: arXiv:2610.39443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a continuous self-map f of a real interval L, let ent(f) denote the supremum of the topological entropies of the restrictions of f to its compact invariant sets; for a compact interval this is the usual topological entropy. For a class P of maps, the entropy spectrum of P is the set of values ent(f) taken by the maps f in P. We determine the entropy spectra of the three standard classes of chaotic maps of the compact interval [0,1]. Devaney chaotic maps have spectrum [(1/2) log 2, infinity], maps of positive entropy have spectrum (0, infinity], and Li-Yorke chaotic maps have spectrum [0, infinity]; thus every entropy compatible with the known lower bounds actually occurs, and the three spectra are strictly nested. Mixing maps have spectrum ((1/2) log 2, infinity], and Devaney chaotic maps with at least two fixed points have spectrum [log 2, infinity]. As a consequence, a Devaney chaotic map of the interval attains the minimal entropy (1/2) log 2 only if it has a unique fixed point and is not mixing. For an arbitrary interval, compact or not, maps with a point of least period n have spectrum [log sigma_n, infinity], where sigma_n are the Stefan constants, and Li-Yorke chaotic maps have spectrum [0, infinity]. The proofs combine a truncation theorem for maps of non-compact intervals, showing that clipping a map to a compact subinterval never creates entropy; a horseshoe argument showing that two fixed points force entropy log 2 on transitive maps; and explicit constructions, including an exact piecewise linear family, a mixing map of infinite entropy, and a square-root construction that halves the entropy of a transitive map.
item.dc:creator: Vinod Kumar P B

item.title: A Sharp Bound of Crossing Limit Cycle for Planar piecewise linear Systems with a Straight Switching Line
item.description: arXiv:2610.39490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the maximum number of crossing limit cycles in planar discontinuous piecewise linear systems separated by a straight line is a central problem in nonsmooth dynamical systems and a natural piecewise-linear counterpart of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, yet its sharp uniform upper bound has long remained an open problem. In this paper, we prove that any such system admits at most three crossing limit cycles. Combined with known examples realizing three crossing limit cycles, this result establishes that three is the sharp uniform upper bound.
item.dc:creator: Zijie Xu, Jiang Yu

item.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.39580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a time-homogeneous Markov process, the fixed-lag solution operator \( (T_\tau f)(x)=\mathbb E[f(X_{t+\tau})\mid X_t=x] \) of the Kolmogorov backward equation evolves observables linearly and deterministically, even when the dynamics are stochastic. We approximate this operator using a two-stage method where we first approximate this operator directly from data, without knowledge of the governing equation (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), and then compress the Galerkin projection onto a finite-dimensional observable space that is fixed in advance or selected variationally. The error analysis traces the learning error of the estimator, the sampling error of the Galerkin inner products, and the invariance and reconstruction properties of the observable space to the computed spectra and forecasts. The sampling error enters only through a multiplicative factor. Near an isolated spectral cluster, the invariance defect of a subspace controls its distance from the target invariant subspace. The forecast error is controlled by the one-step error of the reduced model and the projection error of the observable; when the measure is invariant and the reduced model preserves constants and is stable on mean-zero observables, the bound is uniform in the horizon. For deterministic dynamics, a learning rate for Fourier neural operators (FNOs) gives one explicit bound for the learning error. Numerical experiments illustrate spectral approximation and forecasting, including long-rollout stability and a comparison with extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) when fewer transition pairs than basis functions are observed.
item.dc:creator: Yuanchao Xu, Claire Valva, Ben Gao, Isao Ishikawa

item.title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
item.description: arXiv:2610.39611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results. First, for every wavenumber q in [0.9, 1.1] and every control parameter r between the onset value (1-q^2)^2 and 4, the equation has a nontrivial, real-analytic, odd steady roll; these rolls form a single continuous two-parameter family that bifurcates from the trivial state at onset, with an explicit amplitude bound proportional to the square root of the distance to onset. Second, every roll of this family with r in [0.25, 4] is spectrally unstable on the real line: its linearisation has a Bloch eigenvalue with real part at least 6.7e-4, and at least 0.13 for r >= 0.575. Third, at nine sample points we enclose, at a small Bloch number, the eigenvalue numerically identified with the long-wave (Matthews-Cox) branch; its real part is positive at seven points and negative at two, while strongly unstable eigenvalues exist at all nine. The proofs combine a parametrised Newton-Kantorovich theorem, a desingularisation near onset, Taylor-model bounds on parameter boxes, and a Weyl-sequence argument for the Bloch spectrum; all estimates are evaluated in rigorous interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Nikita V. Konev, Fedor A. Vyazanitsyn, Igor A. Knyazev

item.title: Slow Entropy of Quasi-Unipotent Actions on S-Arithmetic Homogeneous Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study metric and topological slow entropy for translations on a class of finite-volume $S$-arithmetic homogeneous spaces with a real and $p$-adic factor. We consider translations whose real component is quasi-unipotent and whose $p$-adic component lies in a compact open subgroup. At polynomial scales, we show that the metric and topological slow entropies coincide and are determined by the chain structure of the real adjoint action. In particular, the non-Archimedean component contributes no additional polynomial slow entropy. Our result extends the slow entropy formula of Kanigowski, Vinhage, and Wei for quasi-unipotent flows on real homogeneous spaces to this $S$-arithmetic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jasurbek Imomov

item.title: A complete theory of local minimizers for periodic variational problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.39811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the periodic problem in the Calculus of Variations and give a complete characterization of the positive definiteness of the second variation, extending the Reid Roundabout Theorem to periodic boundary conditions. Two formulations are established: one in terms of conjugate and semi-coupled points, and one in terms of the existence of a symmetric solution of the associated Riccati equation satisfying a boundary inequality. We show by an explicit example that the latter condition, while sufficient, is not necessary except in dimension one. As applications, we obtain sufficient conditions for weak and strong local minimizers of periodic solutions of the Euler-Lagrange equation.
item.dc:creator: Marco Fenucci

item.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Thorat

item.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.39928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $\mu$, a $\mu$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Zhao

item.title: Dynamical relations on $\mathbb{P}^1$, higher bifurcations, and arithmetic bigness
item.description: arXiv:2610.40147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study algebraic relations among rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and among their preperiodic points. Working over $\mathbb{C}$, we characterize algebraic families of positive-dimensional varieties in $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ and tuples of maps $(f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ for which the subvariety is dynamically special for a Zariski-dense set of parameters. Moreover, outside of well-understood elliptic phenomena, we show that all families of maps and subvarieties that bifurcate are maximally bifurcating. Working over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we characterize arithmetic and geometric potential bigness for the canonical line bundle associated to families of endomorphisms of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ when restricted to the subvarieties. As consequences, we obtain uniform bounds for the periods and preperiods of relations among non-exceptional maps, and we show uniform bounds on the geometry of preperiodic points satisfying these relations. Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, our results yield corresponding uniform bounds for points and subvarieties satisfying a height gap.
item.dc:creator: Laura DeMarco, Niki Myrto Mavraki

item.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $\Phi = \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(\Phi\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.
item.dc:creator: Jit Wu Yap, Zhuchao Ji

item.title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic
item.description: arXiv:2610.40237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition. As an application, for every $2\leq r<\infty$, we show that the product of the dyadic odometer action of $\mathbb{Z}$ with the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_r$ has a richly ergodic orbit relation, whereas the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_r$ does not. Thus rich ergodicity of a free ergodic action is not determined by the acting group.
item.dc:creator: Wei Dai

item.title: On generic subsystems of a Smale space
item.description: arXiv:2610.40438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study properties of generic compact invariant subsystems of a fixed Smale space in the Hausdorff topology. For a transitive Smale space, we show that the hyperspace of all subsystems contains an open and dense family of NMC subsystems, a dynamically degenerate class with finite orbit structure. A substantially different picture emerges in the closure of the infinite transitive locus: minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero topological entropy are generic, while subsystems conjugate to regular Toeplitz shifts are dense. Despite generic zero entropy, typical subsystems exhibit large oscillations in complexity: we prove that they have infinite slow entropy at the polynomial scale, and their slow entropy at the stretched-exponential scale is equal to one. For mixing Smale spaces, we further study the closure of the infinite totally transitive subsystems. In this hyperspace, minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero entropy remain generic; the conjugacy class of any Sturmian subshift is dense; and uniquely ergodic subsystems whose invariant measure is weakly mixing form a residual set. In particular, topological weak mixing is generic in this space.
item.dc:creator: Angela Flores-Concha (Pennsylvania State University)

item.title: Spontaneous Spirals in Spatial Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.38710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Several chemical and biological systems produce spontaneous spirals in their dynamical behavior, such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction in chemistry and the slime mold Dictyostelium in biology. In a previous study, such spiral wave formation was accurately replicated with a computational spatial system known as the Ideal Storage Cellular Automaton Model (ISCAM). Here, a more detailed investigation is presented of the ability of this model to generate spontaneous spirals depending on its parameter values. A dynamical systems analysis is performed, and bifurcation diagrams, phase space diagrams, and snapshots of the model's spatial dynamics are presented for a range of parameter values. This analysis reveals that spiral waves can only be sustained in the system when the parameter values of the model fall well within the regime of a so-called Neimark-Sacker bifurcation.
item.dc:creator: Wim Hordijk

item.title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.38971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigul\'e and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities. The main step proves that this locus is regular closed off the real axis; this was known for $h=1$ by Calegari, Koch and Walker, for $h\ge19$, and inside an explicit lens. The symmetry $z\mapsto1/z$ then gives the full-plane statement. The proof adapts the method of traps of Calegari, Koch and Walker, using a neighboring-piece criterion, short chains through consecutive digits, and Rouch\'e's theorem. We also classify the convex attractors.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule

item.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.39033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichm\"uller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Corso

item.title: The inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko--Lyubich class
item.description: arXiv:2610.39103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal B$, which is the class of transcendental entire functions with a bounded set of singular values, and its meromorphic generalization $\mathcal B_{mer}$. Every nonempty compact subset of the circle can be the set of Julia limiting directions of an entire $f\in\mathcal B$. For finite unions of nondegenerate closed arcs, the corresponding $f\in\mathcal B$, even with every finite order at or above an explicit bound determined by the arc lengths, can be attained. We also refine the series construction of the latter two authors to obtain $f\in \mathcal B_{mer}$ with any prescribed order and the set of Julia limiting directions.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxing Huang, Jun Wang, Xiao Yao

item.title: Arithmetic localization for quasiperiodic long-range operators with monotone potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.39448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study one-dimensional quasiperiodic operators with $\alpha$-H\"older monotone potentials and long-range hopping satisfying $|T(x,y)|\leq \varepsilon e^{-\rho |x-y|}$. Under an explicit smallness condition on $\varepsilon$, we establish uniform Anderson localization for such operators in the regime $\rho>\alpha\beta $, where $\beta$ is the exponential strength of frequency resonances. Our proof extends the arithmetic localization strategy for monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators by Jitomirskaya and Kachkovskiy to the long-range setting, without relying on the Lyapunov exponent.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Cao

item.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$ with $B_i$ drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$, and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radi\'c, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B+t\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and every $t\ge0$ (respectively $B+B\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B$) is $1/2$ (respectively $3/4$). The main theorem and most of the other results are formalized in Lean 4, with some published theorems entering as explicit hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Shisheng Li, Yong Su

item.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis, Alain Miranville, Tohru Ozawa

item.title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
item.description: arXiv:2610.39820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the period-$3$ condition reduces to $v = -1/(1+u)$, forcing the parameter $t = u$ to satisfy $t, t+1 \in \Z[S^{-1}]^\times$; the template then yields, under ABC, $\max\{|a|,|b|,|a+b|\} \le C_\eps \rad(d)^{1+\eps}$ for $t = a/b$ in lowest terms. We also characterize the period-$3$ locus on the $(u,v)$-plane intrinsically, isolating the ghost curve. Extending the height bound to higher periods remains an open structural question.
item.dc:creator: Antti K\"aenm\"aki, Pekka Kosunen

item.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.
item.dc:creator: Milan Pavlovi\'{c}, Tijana \v{S}ukilovi\'{c}

item.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for P and PSPACE
item.description: arXiv:2610.40025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step. On a fixed compact domain, polynomial time and robust eventual decision characterize P and PSPACE, respectively, with polynomial scale thresholds and no supplied stabilization horizon in the space case. Without sign, floor or conditional primitives, margin amplification at bounded speed, overlapping polynomial gates and interval-product estimates give the common realization, from which we derive shared logical traces, fixed-field PSPACE-complete prediction and a robust safety family with polynomial certificates common to all Euler steps and the flow.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Bournez

item.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.
item.dc:creator: Kohki Sakamoto

item.title: A dynamical approach to Frobenius splitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.40392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A dynamical system can be associated to the process of decomposing iterated Frobenius pushforwards of modules into indecomposable direct summands. Via this connection, we apply the theory of Markov chains to study asymptotic counts of multiplicities of indecomposable summands in the iterated Frobenius pushforwards of the given module, as the number of iterations grows. Our results recover and extend the existing results on the existence of the (generalized) F-signature due to Hashimoto--Symonds, Hashimoto--Kobayashi, Smith--Van den Bergh, Tucker, and Yao. We also develop further the theory of F-contributors, the modules for which the multiplicity grows at the maximal possible rate. As a key algebraic input, we define and develop strongly F-regular modules, extending Hochster--Huneke's notion of strongly F-regular rings. We use strongly F-regular modules to prove convergence of the relevant sequences and algebraically characterize F-contributors, when the underlying ring admits a module-finite strongly F-regular extension or has dimension at most two.
item.dc:creator: Alapan Mukhopadhyay, Ilya Smirnov

item.title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
item.description: arXiv:2610.40426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study introduces a new approach for building surrogate models, in the form of Reduced Order Models (ROMs), for PDE-constrained optimization. A physics-constrained data-driven framework is developed to transform large-scale non-linear optimization problems into ROM-constrained optimization problems. Unlike conventional methods, which suffer from instability of the forward sensitivity function, the proposed approach projects optimization problems to system dynamics optimization problems in Hilbert space to increase stability, diminish memory requirements, and lower computational cost. The present approach is applied to shape optimization of a 2D flapping wing section at $Re=2,400$, where the non-linear interaction of the wing with fluid includes chaotic flow structures. It is shown that the proposed approach can significantly enhance the time-averaged thrust force and propulsive efficiency by 37\% and 40\%, respectively. We also tested this approach for a 3D flapping wing and the results reveal the potential of the proposed approach for more complex optimal designs in the aerospace industry.
item.dc:creator: Hamid R. Karbasian, Brian C. Vermeire

item.title: Bilinear operators along variable curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.40472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by Zygmund's differentiation conjecture and Stein's conjecture for Lipschitz vector fields, we study bilinear singular integral and maximal operators along variable curves given by $$ \begin{aligned} BH_a^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g\left(x + a(x)t^\alpha\right)\,\frac{dt}{t},\\ BM_a^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{2r}\int_{-r}^{r} \left|f(x-t)g\left(x+a(x)t^\alpha\right)\right|\,dt,\\ BSH_c^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.} \int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g(x + t^\alpha)\, \frac{dt}{t-c(x)}, \end{aligned} $$ where $\alpha > 0$ and $a,c:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ are measurable. For every $\alpha>0$ and $0<A<B<\infty$, we construct a smooth, globally Lipschitz coefficient $a:\mathbb R\to(A,B)$ such that, for every H\"{o}lder conjugate pair $1<p,q<\infty$, no strong--type $L^p(\mathbb R)\times L^q(\mathbb R)\to L^1(\mathbb R)$ estimate holds for $BH_a^\alpha$ or $BM_a^\alpha$ on $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\times C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$; moreover, there exist nonnegative smooth inputs in $\bigcap_{s>1}L^s(\mathbb R)$, one of which is compactly supported, whose outputs under $BH_a^\alpha$ and $BM_a^\alpha$ do not belong to $L^1(\mathbb R)$. For any measurable $a:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $BM_a^\alpha$ maps $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R)$ boundedly into $L^r(\mathbb R)$ whenever $1<p,q\leq\infty$, $1/r = 1/p + 1/q$, and $r > 1$, and maps $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R)$ into weak $L^1(\mathbb R)$ when $1/p+1/q=1$, with constants independent of $a$. Finally, we investigate the shifted operator $BSH_c^\alpha$, including dyadic-integer-valued $c$, and prove that there is a measurable choice of $c$ such that the operator admits no bounded $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R) \to L^{r,\infty}(\mathbb R)$ estimates in the range $1 \leq p,q \leq \infty$ and $\frac{1}{2}<r<\infty$, resolving an open problem posed by Gaitan and Lie.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Gismondi, Mandon Pathak

item.title: Classification of critically fixed anti-Thurston maps
item.description: arXiv:2006.10788v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a complete combinatorial classification of critically fixed anti-Thurston maps, i.e., orientation-reversing branched covers of the 2-sphere that fix every critical point. The first step in the proof, and an interesting result in its own right, is a combinatorial classification of critically fixed anti-rational maps as "Schottky maps" associated with certain plane graphs. Both of these classification results heavily rely on an orientation-reversing version of Thurston's theory, including the canonical decomposition of anti-Thurston maps, which we develop in this paper. We use our combinatorial framework to answer special instances of the global curve attractor and twisting problems, and to resolve the Hurwitz existence problem in the setting of critically fixed anti-rational maps. Finally, we give some applications to the study of anti-rational maps with symmetries and to critically fixed anti-polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Geyer, Mikhail Hlushchanka

item.title: The Collatz Conjecture & Non-Archimedean Spectral Theory: Part I -- Arithmetic Dynamical Systems and Non-Archimedean Value Distribution Theory
item.description: arXiv:2007.15936v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime, and let $T_{q}:\mathbb{Z}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ be the Shortened $qx+1$ map, defined by $T_{q}\left(n\right)=n/2$ if $n$ is even and $T_{q}\left(n\right)=\left(qn+1\right)/2$ if $n$ is odd. The study of the dynamics of these maps is infamous for its difficulty, with the characterization of the dynamics of $T_{3}$ being an alternative formulation of the famous Collatz Conjecture. This series of papers presents a new paradigm for studying such arithmetic dynamical systems by way of a neglected area of ultrametric analysis which we have termed $\left(p,q\right)$-adic analysis, the study of functions from the $p$-adics to the $q$-adics, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. In this, the first paper, working with the $T_{q}$ maps as a toy model for the more general theory, for each odd prime $q$, we construct a function $\chi_{q}:\mathbb{Z}_{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{q}$ (the Numen of $T_{q}$) and prove the Correspondence Principle (CP): $x\in\mathbb{Z}\backslash\left\{ 0\right\}$ is a periodic point of $T_{q}$ if and only there is a $\mathfrak{z}\in\mathbb{Z}_{2}\backslash\left\{ 0,1,2,\ldots\right\}$ so that $\chi_{q}\left(\mathfrak{z}\right)=x$.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell Charles Siegel

item.title: A note on $\mathscr{B}$-free sets and the existence of natural density
item.description: arXiv:2506.10218v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $\mathscr{B}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{M}_\mathscr{B}$ be its set of multiples; $\mathscr{B}$ is called Besicovitch if $\mathcal{M}_\mathscr{B}$ has natural density. With $\mathscr{B}$ one associates its tautification $\mathscr{B}'$, the unique taut set with the same Mirsky measure, and the minimal set $\mathscr{B}^*$, which determines the unique minimal subsystem of the $\mathscr{B}$-free subshift. It is known that if $\mathscr{B}'$ is Besicovitch, then so is $\mathscr{B}$. We show that this is the only restriction: all six combinations of the Besicovitch property for $\mathscr{B},\mathscr{B}',\mathscr{B}^*$ compatible with it occur. To this end we prove that every taut set is the tautification of a Besicovitch set, and that every minimal set is the minimal set associated with a Besicovitch taut set. We also show that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathscr{B}'}\setminus\mathcal{M}_\mathscr{B}$ may have positive upper Banach density even if $\mathscr{B}$ and $\mathscr{B}'$ are both Besicovitch in which case this set has zero natural density.
item.dc:creator: Aurelia Dymek, Stanis{\l}aw Kasjan, Joanna Ku{\l}aga-Przymus

item.title: Nonlinear Nonlocal Diffusion Equations for the Analysis of Coordination
item.description: arXiv:2506.13929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coordination games with explicit spatial or relational structure are of interest to economists, ecologists, sociologists, and others studying emergent global properties in collective behavior. When assemblies of individuals seek to coordinate action with one another through myopic best response or other replicator dynamics, the resulting dynamical system can exhibit many rich behaviors. Here we seek to understand these coordination dynamics in the non-atomic setting by use of a nonlinear, nonlocal diffusion equation framework. For this class of nonlocal equations, we prove existence and uniqueness for the initial value problem in the free boundary case and, with certain conditions on the underlying game theory, we go further and prove a maximum principle, weak regularity results, and a characterization of asymptotic behavior. Additionally, with the help of several numerical results, we present several modeling results, characterizing stationary solutions both rigorously and through numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: John S. McAlister, Nina H. Fefferman, Tadele A. Mengesha

item.title: Extreme value theorem for geodesic flow on the quotient of the theta group
item.description: arXiv:2603.07649v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an extreme value theorem for the geodesic flow $g_t$ on the hyperbolic surface $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ associated with the theta group $\Theta$. To capture excursions into both cusps of this surface, we introduce a generalized continued fraction algorithm obtained by splicing the even and odd--odd continued fraction maps into a single dynamical system. We prove that the natural extension of this map is isomorphic to the first return map of the geodesic flow on a suitable cross-section. Using spectral properties of the associated transfer operator, we derive a Galambos-type extreme value law for the digits of the spliced continued fraction. This symbolic result is then translated into a geometric extreme value theorem describing maximal cusp excursions of geodesics on $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Jaelin Kim, Seul Bee Lee, Seonhee Lim

item.title: Bistability, Absolute Concentration Robustness, and Hysteresis in Dual-Site Futile Cycles with Bifunctional Enzymes
item.description: arXiv:2605.11389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bifunctional enzymes, which catalyze both the forward and reverse steps of a substrate modification reaction, arise naturally in bacterial two-component signaling systems and metabolic regulation. Beyond their well-known role in conferring absolute concentration robustness (ACR) on substrate species, bifunctional enzymes profoundly shape the dynamical landscape of the networks in which they appear. We study a class of dual-site futile cycles in which the reverse modification steps are carried out by bifunctional enzyme-substrate compounds, and provide a complete mathematical analysis of all four such networks, characterizing the existence, number, and stability of steady states, as well as the bifurcation structure as total substrate is varied. All four networks admit boundary steady states, in contrast to the non-bifunctional case. The networks differ in the number and stability of boundary steady states, in the maximum number of positive steady states (ranging from two to four), and in whether bistability is present. In two networks, a transcritical bifurcation connects the boundary and positive steady state branches; in one case this is a backward bifurcation, producing hysteresis. Perhaps the most striking phenomenon occurs in one of the four networks, which simultaneously exhibits bistability and ACR in the final modification state, where the system can settle into either of two stable steady states with different intermediate concentrations yet identical final product concentration.
item.dc:creator: Badal Joshi, Tung D. Nguyen, Matthew D. Johnston

item.title: Equilibria in Motion: Stability, Tracking, and Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2606.28422v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: {We study nonautonomous systems whose equilibrium sets are nonisolated and move with time. Their motion is measured on each ball by a localized Attouch--Wets distance, which yields an equilibrium speed that may depend on the radius. The distance from a trajectory to the current equilibrium set is estimated in two ways: through a composite Lyapunov function compared with a power of this distance, and, without any Lyapunov function, through a decay condition on the frozen vector fields. In the first setting, we prove practical stability, and Lyapunov stability when the dissipation has no residual, a case that forces the equilibrium sets to be nested. In the second, we obtain, in the region where the decay condition holds, an explicit tracking estimate driven by the equilibrium speed and the inputs, and we prove asymptotic tracking whenever their averages over unit time intervals vanish, a condition that cannot be weakened among conditions on the speed alone. We also derive input-to-state stability bounds and explicit convergence rates. When the equilibrium speeds are integrable, the equilibrium sets converge in the Attouch--Wets sense to a limiting set at an explicit rate. If, moreover, the velocity is bounded by a multiple of the distance to the current equilibrium set, every trajectory remaining in the region considered has finite length and converges to a point of the limiting set; for a fixed equilibrium set, this yields semistability. The results are illustrated on a scalar example and on resource-allocation models with time-varying demand and with rotating weights.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Saoud

item.title: Equation-Free Screening of Mittag-Leffler-Compatible Dynamics from Scalar Time Series via kNN Multi-Horizon Profiles
item.description: arXiv:2607.08588v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an equation-free screen for finite-window Mittag-Leffler compatibility, in which multihorizon relaxation profiles are constructed out of sample by k-nearest-neighbor prediction from ensembles of scalar trajectories and compared with candidate temporal laws. The screen assesses compatibility, not the generating mechanism. In a matched, noise-free calibration, it reproduces the generating Mittag-Leffler behavior to numerical precision, while relaxation-rate heterogeneity shifts the fitted Mittag-Leffler order toward lower values. For noise-free classical distributed-rate ensembles, a Mittag-Leffler preference over a single exponential disappears when a biexponential alternative is included. Under observational noise, this recovery is incomplete: with three candidate families, the Mittag-Leffler law is still selected in 60% of runs for a classical ensemble, against 72% for a fractional reference. In the tested noise-free settings, simpler profile constructions reproduce the screening decisions, whereas kNN predicts individual trajectories far more accurately than a constant predictor. The screening interpretation of a single-record example, initially investigated as a chaotic test case, is withdrawn as evidence about the continuous system after numerical verification revealed a nonrobust simulated regime. Mittag-Leffler compatibility is therefore a comparative, condition-dependent screening outcome, not identification of fractional origin.
item.dc:creator: N'Gbo N'Gbo, Andrei Velichko, Bruno Carpentieri

item.title: Arithmetic Landscape Functions of a Discrete Cat Map
item.description: arXiv:2607.24857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a permutation of a finite set, we define a landscape by summing a discounted weight over the times each point returns to itself. The landscape value is determined by the point's least period. We relate the trace of the associated resolvent to fixed-point and exact-period counts, and show that the associated determinant is the reciprocal of the Artin-Mazur dynamical zeta function. We apply this framework to the discrete cat map modulo $N$. For every prime $p\ne5$, all nonzero points have period equal to the order of the cat-map matrix modulo $p$, yielding explicit formulas for the landscape trace and determinant. We prove a period-lifting formula at odd primes $p\ne5$, derive exact fixed-point and period counts modulo $5^a$, and combine prime-power results for composite moduli using the Chinese remainder theorem.
item.dc:creator: Aryaman Chandra

item.title: Generic Spectral Determination of Semiclassical Schr\"odinger Operators with $\mathbb Z_2$-Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2608.11111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider the two-dimensional semiclassical Schr\"odinger operator $P_\hbar=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2}\Delta+V$ on $\mathbb R^2$, where $V$ has a nondegenerate well at the origin, its harmonic frequencies are rationally independent, and $V$ is $\mathbb Z_2$-symmetric. We prove that, generically, the first three layers of the quantum Birkhoff normal form (QBNF) determine the full Taylor series of $V$ at the origin, up to the unavoidable spatial inversion $V(x)\mapsto V(-x)$. The generic condition depends only on the jet of $V$ through order ten. Consequently, for real analytic potentials with a unique isolated global well at the origin, the low-lying semiclassical spectrum generically determines $V$ up to spatial inversion.
item.dc:creator: Qiaoling Wei

item.title: Generalized Bratteli diagrams without probability tail invariant measures
item.description: arXiv:2609.14275v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The paper focuses on the following problem: given a generalized Bratteli diagram $B$, determine conditions under which the tail equivalence relation $\mathcal R$ does not admit a tail invariant probability measure on the path space $X_B$. We give several sufficient conditions, formulated in terms of the incidence matrices, that guarantee the nonexistence of such a measure. We also discuss a new spectral method for finding tail invariant measures for a class of stationary generalized Bratteli diagrams. This method allowed us to answer affirmatively an open problem formulated in arXiv:2212.13803.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Barsky, Sergey Bezuglyi

item.title: Existence and Regularity of Stable Resonant Spectral Submanifolds and Linearization Maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.18236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of $C^{r_{*},\alpha}$-regular sub-stable invariant manifolds and conjugacies for analytic maps near a fixed point in the presence of resonances, assuming an invertible semisimple linearization. The regularity order $r$ and the admissible H\"older exponents $\alpha$ depend on the resonant indices and the relative rates of contraction. Our approach uses functional expansions based on logarithmic polynomials, which allow the invariance equation to be solved explicitly and algorithmically to arbitrary order. The existence results are obtained via a fixed-point argument in a suitable Banach space. We further present several analytic examples that illustrate the theorem and demonstrate the loss of regularity caused by resonances.
item.dc:creator: Florian Kogelbauer, Rafael de la Llave

item.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
item.description: arXiv:2609.35632v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic ordering of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex planar central configuration with that ordering, up to similarity. This proves a conjecture of Albouy, Fu and Sun, also called the Sim\'o-Yoccoz conjecture, and answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos. Uniqueness follows by a covering argument from the nondegeneracy of these configurations. We prove nondegeneracy by hand: Dziobek's relations reduce it to an eigenvalue bound for a $2\times2$ matrix that depends only on the shape of the configuration. As consequences, every degenerate planar four-body central configuration is concave, and the known symmetry theorems for kites, isosceles trapezoids and rhombi follow in a few lines.
item.dc:creator: Tejasvi Singh Tomar

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16107v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Combining local boundary analysis, algebraic curves and the computational statements specified in the appendix, we prove that the planar Newtonian five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling for every choice of positive masses. This gives the five-body statement of Smale's sixth problem. We use the singular-sequence classification of Albouy and Kaloshin and resolve the corresponding boundary equations through weighted blow-up charts, rank calculations and local compatibility conditions. For the two remaining diagrams, we prove that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances vanishes. On a hypothetical solution curve containing a positive arc, a pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. A pole of $\Delta$ elsewhere on the completed curve, together with $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$, then contradicts the same local vanishing result. The computational statements for Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 involve exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Canard points in planar mass-action networks: a flux criterion, a duality, and a complete classification
item.description: arXiv:2610.27188v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine which mass-action reaction networks on two species, one fast and one slow, admit a canard point: a singular Hopf bifurcation at a fold of the critical manifold, followed by a canard explosion. In flux coordinates, existence reduces to three linear equations, one linear inequation and a sign condition on the product of two linear forms, and the criticality of the explosion is the sign of an explicit cubic form. For four reactions with a balance matrix of full rank, both become integer polynomial conditions on the stoichiometry. A vacancy duality, which exchanges the activator--inhibitor and substrate-depletion mechanisms, preserves canard points together with their criticality. The central structural result is a mode criterion: a network has a canard point if and only if its elementary flux modes contain a sign-meeting pair and a mode carrying a fold. Hence every canard network contains a minimal one carried by at most three modes, and so by at most twelve reactions, whatever the molecularity. For complexes of molecularity at most three we enumerate all 138\,754 minimal canard networks and label each exactly by the criticalities it admits. None has more than six reactions; 32 have canard points of codimension zero and no explosion; and most six-reaction networks admit both criticalities, separated by degenerate canard points. All labels rest on certificates checked in exact rational arithmetic. Resolving the cubic steps into bimolecular ones through fast dimers keeps the canard points and changes the criticality only by an explicit term.
item.dc:creator: Miruna-Mihaela Beldiman, Andrei-Dan Halanay

item.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.
item.dc:creator: Zhuowei Liu

item.title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
item.description: arXiv:2610.35435v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.
item.dc:creator: Yves Dumont, Marc H\'etier, Valaire Yatat-Djeumen

item.title: Periodic Solutions and Exponential Attractivity in Hopfield-Type Neural Networks with Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive and Nonimpulsive Cases
item.description: arXiv:2610.36560v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by $\gamma(t)=\zeta_k$ on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, where $t_k\leq\zeta_k\leq t_{k+1}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Depending on the position of $\zeta_k$, the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type. By representing periodic solutions through a Green function and applying a fixed-point argument, we obtain explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an $\omega$-periodic solution. We then use a Gronwall-type estimate, together with period averages, to prove that this solution is globally exponentially attractive. These conditions can be checked directly from the system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution. In the course of the analysis, we also revisit and correct some estimates presented by Pinto et al. \cite{Pinto_ejqtde}. The case $\zeta_k=t_k$ reduces to their setting, whereas our results cover the more general choice of $\zeta_k$ within each interval. We also present examples illustrating different types of piecewise constant arguments.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Torres Naranjo, Samuel Castillo Apolonio

item.title: Irreducible groups and ergodicity in the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2512.12141v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that if $G$ is a real semi-simple Lie group, and $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of $G$ containing a subgroup $\Sigma$ acting ergodically (in a strong sense) on the Furstenberg boundary of $G$, then $\Gamma$ is not isomorphic to a free product of $\Sigma$ with $\mathbb{Z}$. Moreover, if $\Sigma$ has algebraic entries, then $\Gamma$ has algebraic entries as well. As a consequence, we show that if all irreducible discrete subgroups of ${\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ act ergodically on $\mathbb{S}^1\times \mathbb{S}^1 $, such groups cannot be free groups (or even Gromov hyperbolic). In the appendix, we discuss a connection between the existence of discrete irreducible groups and diophantine properties of Lie groups.
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Dey, Sebastian Hurtado

item.title: Szemer\'edi's Theorem Along Cantor Sets of Integers
item.description: arXiv:2602.15299v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal C= \{k_1<k_2 < \cdots\}$ be Cantor set of integers, that is a set of integers with restricted digits modulo a base $b$, and suppose $0$ is one of the restricted digits. We show that $$ \liminf_{M-N\to\infty}\mathbb E _{n\in [N]- [M]} m(A\cap T^{-k_n} A \cap \cdots \cap T^{-\ell k_n} A )>0. $$ The averages above are uniform in the index $n$, and so the set of indices $n$ for which $m(A\cap T^{-k_n} A \cap \cdots \cap T^{-\ell k_n} A )>0$ is syndetic. By the Furstenberg correspondence principle, it follows that for every set of integers $A$ of positive upper Banach density there is a syndetic set $B$ of indices such that, for each $n \in B$, the set of $a$ with $a, a+k_n, \ldots, a+ \ell k_n \in A$ again has positive upper Banach density. A Cantor set contains an IP-set, so the existence of such progressions, and the positivity of the density above for a single index, already follow from the IP Szemer\'edi theorem of Furstenberg and Katznelson, and from the work of Kra and Shalom. The point of this paper is instead the frequency with which the step sizes $k_n$ may be found, measured in the natural enumeration of the Cantor set itself.
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, Michael T. Lacey, Dario Mena, Maria Carmen Reguera

item.title: Rational Preperiodic Points of Quadratic Rational Maps over $\mathbb{Q}$ with Nonabelian Automorphism Groups
item.description: arXiv:2603.06203v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ be a quadratic rational map defined over the rational field $\mathbb{Q}$ with nonabelian automorphism group. We prove that no such map has a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational periodic point with exact period $N\ge 4$. We also give an explicit parametrization of such maps that have $\mathbb{Q}$-rational periodic points of exact period $1$, $2$, and $3$. In addition, we show that the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational preperiodic points of such a map $f$ cannot exceed $6$. As a result, we completely classify all portraits of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational preperiodic points for quadratic rational maps defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ with nonabelian automorphism group, showing that there are exactly $7$ such portraits, one of which is the empty portrait.
item.dc:creator: Hasan Bilgili, Mohammad Sadek

item.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
item.description: arXiv:2610.37372v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. For responses whose rare-predator limit is strictly increasing and whose value at positive predator density never exceeds that limit, we also establish necessity of positive predator invasion whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If the prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity itself forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth. Logistic and bounded saturating growth laws provide explicit Gamma and beta-prime resident distributions. Applications include Holling, Ivlev, Beddington-DeAngelis, and Crowley-Martin responses. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share the coexistence threshold, although predator interference changes the interior distribution. Reproducible quadrature and simulations illustrate this distinction. The analysis builds on existing stochastic persistence theory and identifies precisely the additional comparison argument needed for necessity, including exclusion of interior invariant measures at zero predator invasion.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es S\'anchez, Leon A. Valencia, Jorge M. Ramirez Osorio
